facts.fact: The Finance Ministry communique of 10 April 2026, as reported by LeFisk, says the DGI's ATOM platform has been in service since 1 July 2026 and is mandatory for all new registrations, issuing the NIU taxpayer number online.

LeFisk reports that ATOM is progressively replacing the Harmony platform, with taxpayers already registered on Harmony required to re-register on ATOM between 1 July and 31 December 2026, after which only ATOM registrations are valid.

facts.fact: The Directorate General of Taxation says tax registration is done exclusively online by the taxpayer, and the computer system allots a unique taxpayer number (NIU) automatically.
The Directorate General of Taxation says registrants must give and attach their national identity card number, and the administration checks the identifying details against the attached documents.

facts.fact: Business in Cameroon reports the Finance Minister approved on 10 April 2026 a EUR 5.997m contract for SIGIT, a new tax management system that will support taxpayer registration, with 24 months of implementation under the KfW-financed PMSI-DGI programme.
